entry.title: Pipfolio: Pip-Boy Inspired Web Portfolio
entry.summary:
This is a submission for the New Year, New You Portfolio Challenge Presented by Google AI First and foremost, I'm a big Fallout fan, specifically Fallout: New Vegas. As proven by my playtime on Steam:
With the current ongoing season of the Fallout adaptation TV show centered around New Vegas, I could not think of a better theme for my new portfolio to show off my skills as well as my interest in a single glance. Here's the live website: https://pip-boy-portfolio-978859030334.us-west1.run.app Here's the repo if you're interested: https://github.com/AnsellMaximilian/pip-boy-portfolio I built this entirely using Google's AI Studio. I must say it went very well. I'll give you the exact first prompt I gave it word for word. No planning; just natural language:
As you can see, I kept it simple at first just so I could see the design it would cook up and, if needed, adjust if I weren't satisfied. Crucially, I gave it sample images of the actual Pip-Boy to give it some inspiration:
The current app looks a lot more advanced that what this first prompt created, but thanks to AI Studio's version history feature, I can show you exactly what it built the first time around:
As you can see; it's already pretty good. But it was far from finished. So after a few more prompts and adjustment... I ended with something like this:
To look at the full thing, make sure to visit the deployed version above. AI Studio really got it perfect at the start. The theme, colors, and the terminal effects all really sell the vibes well. I tried to get it to maintain that design to the very end, and it worked great! I really like the contacts section disguised as the "Radio" menu in the Pip-Boy:
Something cool that happened during development: I basically gave a link to my old portfolio website and asked it to parse it and put my skills there into the S.P.E.C.I.A.L section in the Pipfolio, and it did exactly that.

entry.title: Claude Code costs up to $200 a month. Goose does the same thing for free.
entry.summary: The artificial intelligence coding revolution comes with a catch: it's expensive. Claude Code, Anthropic's terminal-based AI agent that can write, debug, and deploy code autonomously, has captured the imagination of software developers worldwide. But its pricing — ranging from $20 to $200 per month depending on usage — has sparked a growing rebellion among the very programmers it aims to serve. Now, a free alternative is gaining traction. Goose, an open-source AI agent developed by Block (the financial technology company formerly known as Square), offers nearly identical functionality to Claude Code but runs entirely on a user's local machine. entry.title: Listen Labs raises $69M after viral billboard hiring stunt to scale AI customer interviews
entry.summary: Alfred Wahlforss was running out of options. His startup, Listen Labs, needed to hire over 100 engineers, but competing against Mark Zuckerberg's $100 million offers seemed impossible. So he spent $5,000 — a fifth of his marketing budget — on a billboard in San Francisco displaying what looked like gibberish: five strings of random numbers. The numbers were actually AI tokens. Decoded, they led to a coding challenge: build an algorithm to act as a digital bouncer at Berghain, the Berlin nightclub famous for rejecting nearly everyone at the door. Within days, thousands attempted the puzzle. 430 cracked it. Some got hired. The winner flew to Berlin, all expenses paid. That unconventional approach has now attracted $69 million in Series B funding, led by Ribbit Capital with participation from…
